description: Branch R-SORT-3 Shortened-key collisions (public side), one expanding character kind per probe (this one: U+00DF, 1 unit(s) per repetition, on a ACCDB), repairing the single earlier case where SQL equality called two different 255-unit keys equal. L(ID, K Text(255)) has non-unique IX_K built before the rows and L0 is an unindexed copy. Rows: IDs 1 and 2 = the character repeated to 254 units + 'x' and + 'y'; IDs 3 and 4 the same with 200 units (a control well inside the limit); ID 5 = 'y' + the 254-unit head (a change at the first unit). Reads on L and on L0: GROUP BY K (first ID, count) in key order; ORDER BY K, ID; the equality join A.K = B.K where A.ID < B.ID; the join A.K < B.K where A.ID + 1 = B.ID; WHERE K = (the key of ID 1). On L the table-type Seek on IX_K for the keys of IDs 1 and 2 with = (NoMatch and the current ID) and > (the current ID), and the IX_K walk. A unique index UX_K on a second table UL with the same rows is loaded with a marked Errors read per row. Asks whether the engine ever calls the two keys equal (by index, join, subquery or Seek), orders them inconsistently, or refuses the second as a duplicate, with and without an index.

args.text: CREATE TABLE L (ID LONG CONSTRAINT PK_L PRIMARY KEY, K TEXT(255))
CREATE TABLE UL (ID LONG CONSTRAINT PK_UL PRIMARY KEY, K TEXT(255))
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX UX_K ON UL (K)
CREATE TABLE L0 (ID LONG CONSTRAINT PK_L0 PRIMARY KEY, K TEXT(255))
INSERT INTO L0 (ID, K) SELECT ID, K FROM L
SELECT MIN(ID), COUNT(*) FROM L GROUP BY K ORDER BY K
SELECT ID FROM L ORDER BY K, ID
SELECT A.ID, B.ID FROM L AS A INNER JOIN L AS B ON A.K = B.K WHERE A.ID < B.ID
SELECT A.ID, B.ID FROM L AS A INNER JOIN L AS B ON A.K < B.K WHERE A.ID + 1 = B.ID
SELECT ID FROM L WHERE K = (SELECT K FROM L WHERE ID = 1) ORDER BY ID
SELECT MIN(ID), COUNT(*) FROM L0 GROUP BY K ORDER BY K
SELECT ID FROM L0 ORDER BY K, ID
SELECT A.ID, B.ID FROM L0 AS A INNER JOIN L0 AS B ON A.K = B.K WHERE A.ID < B.ID
SELECT A.ID, B.ID FROM L0 AS A INNER JOIN L0 AS B ON A.K < B.K WHERE A.ID + 1 = B.ID
SELECT ID FROM L0 WHERE K = (SELECT K FROM L0 WHERE ID = 1) ORDER BY ID
SELECT ID FROM UL ORDER BY ID
